Or may be it actually worked as expected as one out of memory event may have killed multiple tasks at once. See https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5985077141

We also must make sure that on recovery from out of memory even we don't do it all at the same time and have some random interval from 30 to 90 seconds, so we reduce probability everything will come rushing access all the same resources at once.

May be we should also update to the latest versions of all dependencies + check that https://github.com/link-foundation/start has exactly all the features we need.

Thanks for the review. I checked all three points; full details are in [the case study, "Follow-up: owner feedback on PR #2499"](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2498-69233edb3b6c/docs/case-studies/issue-2498/README.md#follow-up-owner-feedback-on-pr-2499).

**1. Did one OOM event kill several tasks at once?** Partly yes, but they were not one shared event, and that is not what stopped the sessions.
- I downloaded the full meta-language#196 log ([excerpt with the key lines](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2498-69233edb3b6c/docs/case-studies/issue-2498/meta-language-196-log-excerpt.txt)). It shows 5 `formal-ai-corpus-memory` runs `Killed` (exit 137): 2 reported at 19:37:53 and 3 at 19:44:03.
- In package-registry-manager#27, `rustc` was killed at 19:38:41.
- Each task container is capped at `DEFAULT_DOCKER_TASK_MEMORY=25%` of the 11.7 GB host, which is **2.9 GB**. The resource snapshots kept host memory at 4.6–6.7 GB available the whole time. So these were separate, one-after-another kills at each container's own 2.9 GB limit, not one host-wide event.
- The kill notice said "10.4 GB of 11.7 GB available". That is host RAM, which is why the meta-language audit read it as an "11.7 GB limit".
- Both sessions ended for the same reason, 3½ minutes apart: the shared Claude OAuth token could not be refreshed (19:40:42 and 19:44:03). That stop is what this PR stops reporting as an OOM kill.
- To answer this directly next time, every resource snapshot now records the container's cgroup:
  - `memory.max`, `memory.current` and `memory.peak`;
  - `memory.events` `oom` and `oom_kill`.
  The kill diagnosis quotes these values. `oom_kill > 1` means several processes were killed; `oom_kill > oom` points to a host-wide OOM rather than the container limit.

**2. Random 30–90 s delay before recovery: done.**
- Every automatic recovery now waits its own random delay before it starts, whether it is a monitor-driven recovery (in place or in a fresh session) or solve's in-process resume after a tool OOM kill.
- The default is 30–90 s. Set it with `--session-kill-resume-delay <min-max>` or `HIVE_MIND_SESSION_KILL_RESUME_DELAY`; `0` turns it off.
- Each session has its own in-flight guard, so one session's wait does not hold up the others.
- The new tests are in `tests/issue-2498-recovery-delay.test.mjs`.

**3. Dependencies and start-command.**
- `npm outdated` is empty for the direct dependencies. `start-command@0.35.1` and `@link-assistant/agent@0.26.11` are the latest releases.
- start covers what hive-mind uses. I reported the gaps upstream:
  - link-foundation/start#180: `memoryExhausted` is taken from Docker's sticky `OOMKilled` flag;
  - link-foundation/start#181: `--on-kill-resume` has no random delay (hive-mind does not use it, but other users would hit the same rush);
  - link-foundation/start#182: `--status` should report the cgroup `oom`/`oom_kill`/peak counters.
